---
name: work-status
description: 'Reports where the project''s work items stand: progress, blockers, the next item, and decisions waiting on the owner. Use whenever the owner asks about project or item status, even one item, for example "where are we", "what''s next", or "is X done yet". Not for a chat recap; use session-summary.'
---

# Work status

Voice: write to the owner in plain English. Claude Code: follow the project's Plain English output style. Codex: follow the "How to write replies" section of `AGENTS.md`.
Reports where the work stands. This skill only reads: apart from the CLI's own sync (the history rows it writes for the owner's hand moves), it never changes an item, memory, or a file.

## Steps

1. Use the project briefing when this conversation has it and nothing changed since. Otherwise run it.
   `toolkit brief`
2. The owner named an item or an area: answer about that item only. Where it stands in plain words, what is done and left in its Roadmap, its blockers, and its next action.
   `toolkit work show <id>`
3. The whole project: read the tree, the recommended next item, the decisions waiting on the owner, and the current focus.
   `toolkit work list --tree`
   `toolkit work next`
   `toolkit work decisions`
   `toolkit memory focus`
4. Answer in the order and shape in "How to answer" below. Say every stage in plain words with the item id ("WI-012 is in testing"); the labels come from the lifecycle.
   `toolkit work lifecycle`
5. For each problem, name the skill that fixes it, without running it: moved or missing items, `work-organize`; setup warnings, `project-setup`; decisions, `work-decide`.
6. "Show the board": local tracker, summarize `.work-items/DASHBOARD.md`; Notion, give the Work Items link (`references/tracker-notion.md`, "The board link").
   `toolkit config get notion.workItems.url`
7. End with one thing the owner can say next, for example "Say 'what do you need from me' to go through the 2 decisions."

## Gotchas

- Run each `toolkit` command alone: never joined by `&&`, `;`, or a pipe, and never from a script (in Codex that runs it inside the sandbox, where it fails; `references/toolkit-commands.md`).
- "Agent to-do" lines in the decisions list are the agent's own steps, not decisions. Count and show only the decisions.
- Archived items are hidden from the briefing and the recommended next item. Mention them only when the owner asks.
- GitHub Issues or Jira: `toolkit work` exits with code 3. Read the issues with the tracker's own tool (`references/tracker-github.md` or `references/tracker-jira.md`, section "The `toolkit work` steps") and answer in the same order.
- Nothing is tracked yet: say so in one line and offer `work-on` for the first piece of work.

## How to answer

- Lead with the answer, not with how you found it.
- Decisions first, because only the owner can unblock them: the count, then one line each with the item id, what is being decided, and how long it has waited when the record shows it.
- One line per item in progress: id, title, plain stage, what is left, and who it waits on.
- The recommended next item and why, in one line.
- Recently done: items finished since the last session, when the record shows it. Skip it when there are none.
- Anything moved or broken, with the skill that fixes it.
- Keep it short. The owner can ask about one item for detail.

Example:

```markdown
2 decisions wait on you:
- WI-012: approve the CSV export result (waiting since 2026-09-26).
- WI-015: choose design A (built-in report) or B (custom page).

In progress:
- WI-014 "Nightly sync", in build (stage 08): P2 of 3 left; waiting on nobody.

Next: WI-016 "Login page copy", because it blocks the release and needs no decision.

Say "what do you need from me" to go through the 2 decisions.
```

## Not this skill

- "What did we do in this chat": `session-summary`.
- "What do you need from me": `work-decide`, which walks through each decision.
- "What did we decide about X": `memory-find`.

Stages (the status follows the stage):
  01-discovery              Backlog      Working out what the owner wants.                                    Continue with: work-requirements
  02-refinement             Backlog      Turning that into requirements.                                      Continue with: work-requirements
  03-requirements-approved  Ready        The owner approved the requirements.                                 Continue with: solution-design or work-on
  04-solution-design        In Progress  Deciding how it gets built.                                          Continue with: solution-design
  05-breakdown              In Progress  Splitting work that is too large.                                    Continue with: work-organize
  06-implementation-plan    In Progress  Ordering the build steps.                                            Continue with: work-on
  07-tracking-setup         In Progress  Creating build tracking when needed.                                 Continue with: work-on
  08-build                  In Progress  Producing the requested change.                                      Continue with: work-on
  09-testing                In Progress  Checking it against the requirements.                                Continue with: work-check
  10-bug-fixing             In Progress  Fixing what testing found.                                           Continue with: work-check
  11-user-approval          In Progress  The owner reviews the result.                                        Continue with: work-check
  12-pr-and-push            In Review    Repository work is in a pushed pull request.                         Continue with: work-finish
  13-deployment             In Review    The result is put where it belongs.                                  Continue with: work-finish
  14-spec-update            In Review    Lasting specifications match the result.                             Continue with: work-finish
  (Done)                    Done         Set only by toolkit work finish <id> --by <name> --evidence <text>.  Continue with: nothing (finished)
  (Cancelled)               Cancelled    Set only by toolkit work cancel <id> --reason <text>.                Continue with: nothing (finished)
  An item with waiting_on: owner continues with work-decide, whatever its stage.

Statuses:
  Backlog      Logged; requirements are still being worked out (stages 01-02).
  Ready        Requirements approved; work can start (stage 03).
  In Progress  The item is active (stages 04-11). It does not mean building has started.
  In Review    The result is in a pull request, being deployed, or being written into the specifications (stages 12-14).
  Done         The owner accepted the result. Set only by toolkit work finish.
  Cancelled    Work stopped without the result. Set only by toolkit work cancel.

Types:
  discovery               Finding out what is needed.
  solution-design         Designing how something gets built.
  build                   Producing a change. Needs approved requirements before stage 03.
  data-load               Loading or changing data. Needs approved requirements before stage 03.
  repository-maintenance  Keeping the repository in order.
  research                Answering a question with sources.
  task                    A small piece of work.
  bug                     Something that does not work as it should.
  enhancement             An improvement to something that works.
  Other lower-case words are allowed as types.

Priorities: urgent, high, medium, low. Waiting on: owner, agent, external: <who>, none. Delivery: agent-led, owner-led, not-offered.

Approval gates:
  Requirements approval: asked by work-requirements; recorded with toolkit work approve <id> --requirements --by <name>. build and data-load items cannot reach stage 03 or later without it. Sets stage 03 when the item is earlier.
  Design approval: asked by solution-design; recorded with toolkit work approve <id> --design --by <name>. The design stays proposed until the owner approves it.
  Result approval (stage 11): asked by work-check; recorded with toolkit work approve <id> --result --by <name>. The owner approves the result before it is finished.
  Done: asked by work-finish; recorded with toolkit work finish <id> --by <name> --evidence <text> [--quote <owner's words>]. Only this command sets Done. With no recorded result approval it needs --quote, the owner's own words approving the result, and records that approval.
  Cancel: asked by work-finish; recorded with toolkit work cancel <id> --reason <text>. Only this command sets Cancelled. The reason is the owner's words.
  Delivery offer and team: asked by work-delegate; recorded with toolkit work set <id> --delivery agent-led|owner-led. Offered once per goal; the detail goes in Notes > Decisions and context.
  Project-wide decision: asked by work-decide; recorded with toolkit decision add --decision <text> --why <text> --by <name>. A row in DECISIONS.md at the project root.

What counts as approval:
  - Only the owner's explicit words count as approval. Quote them in the record.
  - A question, a suggestion, a tentative answer, or a saved draft is not approval.
  - Approval never covers merge, deployment, spending, or publishing.
  - Approval survives later stages. A stage alone does not prove approval: check the approval field.
  - A hand change that skips a gate is kept and reported as a question for the owner. It is never reverted.

Rules:
  - Status follows stage: 01-02 Backlog, 03 Ready, 04-11 In Progress, 12-14 In Review.
  - Stages may be skipped, repeated, and revisited. Record a one-line reason when a move is not obvious.
  - Pull-request stages (12) apply only to repository work.
  - Blocking is waiting_on plus the Overview Blockers line, never a status.
  - An item waiting on the owner continues with work-decide, whatever its stage.
  - An item that breaks an approval gate continues with work-decide until the owner answers.
  - An item at 11 User approval whose result approval is recorded continues with work-finish.
  - A Done or Cancelled item continues with nothing: it is finished. Reopen it with toolkit work set <id> --stage <s> --reopen.
